title: OS Finals Reviewer

modules.title: Storage Systems, Hard Disks, SAN, NAS, & RAID
Network Directory Services, File Sharing, & Permissions
System Security, Policies, Authentication, & Backup Strategies

questions.prompt: Your manager has asked you to terminate a process running on a Linux server. Before you can terminate the process, what information do you need?
questions.explanation: When a process is created, the operating system assigns it a unique Process ID (PID). You must use this identifier with commands like kill to locate and terminate the specific process.

questions.prompt: While on a coffee break, your colleague asserts that cooperative multitasking is the best operating system design. What is your response? (Choose three.)

choices.text: A disadvantage of cooperative multitasking is that it relies on each program to decide when to give control back to the operating system.
Cooperative multitasking can be faster than other forms of multitasking because it increases the clock speed of the processor.
Cooperative multitasking OSs can freeze due to a process getting stuck in an infinite loop.
Modern operating systems use preemptive multitasking so that the operating system is fully in control.
Cooperative multitasking is best used on real-time operating systems.

questions.explanation: In cooperative multitasking, applications must voluntarily yield CPU time. If poorly written software enters an infinite loop, it will not yield, causing the whole system to lock up. Modern OSs prevent this by using preemptive multitasking, which ensures the kernel retains the authority to force a switch between running processes.
questions.answerText: a. A disadvantage of cooperative multitasking is that it relies on each program to decide when to give control back to the operating system.; c. Cooperative multitasking OSs can freeze due to a process getting stuck in an infinite loop.; d. Modern operating systems use preemptive multitasking so that the operating system is fully in control.

questions.prompt: A friend of yours described a program he is writing that runs on a microcontroller and will read sensors and write to devices that control industrial equipment. What type of system is his program most likely working with?
questions.explanation: Industrial controllers and sensor-driven microcontrollers are typical embedded systems, which are dedicated to specific control functions rather than general-purpose computing tasks.

questions.prompt: Which method of I/O handling uses a round-robin technique?
questions.explanation: Polling operates by sequentially checking the status of each I/O device in a continuous round-robin cycle to see if it requires attention from the CPU.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is performed by the BIOS? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: The basic input/output system (BIOS) runs diagnostic hardware tests at startup, known as the power-on self-test (POST). Following the POST, the BIOS uses its bootstrap program to locate the bootloader, which is then responsible for starting the operating system.
questions.answerText: a. runs the power-on self-test, b. starts the operating system

questions.prompt: Which type of operating system is most likely to be part of an embedded system?
questions.explanation: Embedded systems in industrial or mission-critical environments often require real-time operating systems (RTOS) because they guarantee immediate, deterministic responses to physical hardware events.

questions.prompt: A new application you are installing is critical to business operations and downtime is to be avoided. In addition, fast response times are necessary, so performance must be scaled when more users start using the system. What OS and server hardware feature should you consider implementing on the system on which the application is installed?
questions.explanation: Server clustering combines multiple servers into a single logical system. This provides fault tolerance to prevent downtime if one hardware node fails, and it allows for load balancing to scale performance as user traffic increases.

questions.prompt: You are asked to develop a process that runs in the background and handles network communications. What type of process should you develop?
questions.explanation: Services (often called daemons in Linux) are processes designed to run quietly in the background without a user interface, making them ideal for continuous tasks like managing network communications.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is best to run on a client operating system?
questions.explanation: Client operating systems are explicitly optimized for running foreground applications requested by a user, such as a web browser. Technologies like DHCP servers, Active Directory, and host virtualization platforms are intended for server operating systems.

questions.prompt: A colleague asks you where the code for the power-on self-test is located. What do you tell her?
questions.explanation: The POST code is part of the system's firmware (BIOS or UEFI), which is permanently stored on the motherboard in non-volatile memory chips such as flash memory or EEPROM.

questions.prompt: Which component of the operating system gets called when a process must be allocated memory and scheduled to run?
questions.explanation: The kernel is the core component of an operating system responsible for managing low-level hardware interactions, including dynamically allocating memory and scheduling CPU time for processes.

questions.prompt: You're writing a program that must enable and disable interrupts. In which CPU mode must your program operate?
questions.explanation: Enabling and disabling hardware interrupts are highly privileged operations. To prevent malicious or accidental system crashes, these tasks are restricted strictly to kernel mode.

questions.prompt: Which of the following best describes the MS-DOS operating system?
questions.explanation: Early operating systems like MS-DOS are classified as standalone because they were built for single users and single tasks, and were not originally designed to access network resources or interact natively with other systems.

questions.prompt: Which of the following are you most likely to find in firmware?
questions.explanation: System firmware contains the initial bootstrap program, which executes upon startup to locate and load the operating system's bootloader into memory.

questions.prompt: Which aspect of security and protection services verifies that an account has permission to perform an action on an operating system?
questions.explanation: While authentication confirms a user's identity, authorization is the subsequent security process that verifies whether the authenticated account actually has the necessary permissions to perform an action or access a file.

questions.prompt: You have been asked to recommend an operating system for a project that requires precise timing of I/O devices and deterministic response times to events. Which OS should you recommend?
questions.explanation: VxWorks is a recognized real-time operating system (RTOS) designed specifically to handle precise timing and guaranteed deterministic responses. Options like Linux and Android are general-purpose operating systems.

questions.prompt: Which of the following executes instructions provided by computer programs?
questions.explanation: The Central Processing Unit (CPU) is the primary hardware component responsible for processing and physically executing the operational instructions provided by software programs.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is a feature typically provided by an operating system? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: The file system and kernel are fundamental, built-in structural components of an operating system that manage disk storage and hardware access. Spreadsheets and database apps are third-party software applications installed by users.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is a basic function all computers perform? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: At a fundamental architectural level, all computing devices accept data (input), manipulate or calculate that data (processing), and present the result (output).
questions.answerText: a. processing; d. input; f. output

questions.prompt: Which of the following are ways that a process is created? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: The initial fundamental OS processes are loaded and started by the bootloader during system startup. Following boot, user actions—such as typing a command in a terminal or double-clicking an application icon—signal the operating system to spawn new processes.
questions.answerText: a. by the bootloader, d. by the user

questions.prompt: What is the default authentication protocol used by Windows 2000 Server and later versions?
questions.explanation: Kerberos is a security system and authentication protocol that authenticates users and grants or denies access to network resources based on a user's log-on name and password.

questions.prompt: What are the two main design standards to which most versions of UNIX adhere? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: Contemporary versions of UNIX adhere to either the Berkeley Software Distribution (BSD) standard or the System V Release 4 (SVR4) standard.

questions.prompt: Which of the following best describes Hyper-V?

choices.text: the fifth version of the overdrive section on the Intel chip
a method to increase the speed of memory access on a personal computer
the server virtualization service used to create multiple logical servers on one physical server
extremely fast communication over the USB port

questions.explanation: Hyper-V is a hypervisor service that enables Windows Server to host multiple virtual machines, providing OS and application isolation alongside server consolidation.
questions.answerText: c. the server virtualization service used to create multiple logical servers on one physical server

questions.prompt: What does it mean if a driver is signed?

choices.text: The driver file contains a digital certificate.
Only certified versions of the driver can be installed.
The driver can only work in Windows 10 and later versions.
The driver must be installed on a server.

questions.explanation: Driver signing ensures that only certified versions of drivers can be installed, which prevents them from being inadvertently overwritten by earlier versions and provides security against malware-infested drivers.
questions.answerText: b. Only certified versions of the driver can be installed.

questions.prompt: Looking at Windows Server 2012 R2, which of the following statements is true?

choices.text: It was released in both a 32-bit and 64-bit version.
It shares a core operating system with Windows Vista.
It supports virtual machines with up to 32 GB of RAM.
It has group policy features that only work with Windows XP clients.

questions.explanation: Hyper-V 3.0, included in Windows Server 2012, supports virtual machines with up to 32 GB of RAM and up to 32 virtual processors.
questions.answerText: c. It supports virtual machines with up to 32 GB of RAM.

questions.prompt: You have a Web server that contains primarily static data. The server is heavily used and response times are getting longer. What can you do to mitigate the increasing response times?

choices.text: Use a hypervisor to increase performance.

questions.explanation: Network load-balancing (NLB) clusters share incoming service requests based on administrator rules. They are ideal for TCP/IP-based applications such as Web servers where data is easily replicated and not changed by users.
questions.answerText: d. Create a network load-balancing cluster.

questions.prompt: What feature can you use starting in Windows Server 2012 if you want to be able to assign file and folder permissions based on user attributes and the contents of the file?
questions.explanation: Dynamic Access Control allows files to be classified based on their data contents and enables the assignment of permissions using user attributes instead of relying on traditional group memberships.

questions.prompt: What was the original Microsoft operating system for the IBM PC?
questions.explanation: Introduced in 1981, MS-DOS 1.0 was Microsoft's original operating system designed for the IBM PC hardware platform.

questions.prompt: Which Debian-based distribution of Linux is ideal for learning about cybersecurity because of its wide collection of forensic and security tools?
questions.explanation: Kali Linux is based on Debian and is widely favored by students of cybersecurity because it contains a broad collection of forensic and security tools.

questions.prompt: What is the command-line interface called on a Linux system?
questions.explanation: After a user is verified on a Linux system, they are presented with a shell, which serves as the user interface and functions similarly to a Windows command prompt.

questions.prompt: You have a branch office with limited physical security for your servers. You want domain users in the office to be able to be authenticated by a local server, but you are concerned that the server might be compromised or stolen due to the lack of physical security. What should you do?
questions.explanation: A read-only domain controller (RODC) authenticates users but restricts hackers from making local changes that would replicate back to the main domain controller. It also limits the amount of sensitive information stored on the server, making it ideal for locations with limited security like branch offices.

questions.prompt: Windows 2000 Server was the first Windows server to have the Active Directory service. True or False?
questions.explanation: Active Directory was initially introduced in Windows 2000 Server and remains the fundamental component of a Windows domain environment.

questions.prompt: You have been asked to install Windows Server 2012 on a server that has limited memory and disk space. You need to ensure that the installation has as small a footprint as possible; also, the server will be managed using remote server administration tools or the command line. How can you accomplish this?

choices.text: Install Hyper-V Server with Windows Server 2012 as a VM.
Install a compressed version of Windows Server 2012 R2.
Install a Linux hypervisor and then install Windows Server 2012.
Install Windows Server 2012 but choose the Server Core option.

questions.explanation: Server Core is a minimal installation option with a lightweight interface that lacks a resource-intensive GUI, allowing a fresh installation to utilize little more than 5 GB of disk space. Most configurations are done via the command prompt, PowerShell, or remote administration tools.
questions.answerText: d. Install Windows Server 2012 but choose the Server Core option.

questions.prompt: Which Windows feature, introduced in Windows 95, helped eliminate device resource conflicts and precluded manual device configuration with jumpers?
questions.explanation: Plug and Play (PnP) empowered the operating system to automatically detect and configure hardware via software, eliminating the difficulties of manual configuration using expansion card or motherboard jumpers.

questions.prompt: What technology was implemented on Apple computer printer ports to facilitate file and printer sharing?
questions.explanation: Apple integrated LocalTalk networking hardware with all Macintosh printer ports to provide an inexpensive interface that combined networking and serial connectivity.

questions.prompt: With which client OS did Windows Server 2008 share the same code base?
questions.explanation: Windows Server 2008 and Windows Vista shared the same code base and consequently possessed the same new features.

questions.prompt: Which Windows feature made the use of chkdsk.exe much less common?
questions.explanation: Self-healing NTFS operates in the background to automatically correct hard disk errors, whereas previously administrators had to take the volume offline to utilize the Chkdsk.exe utility.

questions.prompt: Your boss has informed you that three aging servers must be replaced with a single physical server. However, you have found that two of the servers are running 64-bit applications that conflict with one another and cannot be installed on the same OS. Do you have a solution for this problem?

choices.text: Install Windows Server 2016 with Hyper-V and create three VMs, each running Windows Server 2016.
Install Windows Server Core on three hard disk partitions and create a multi-boot system.
Install Windows Server 2019 and use WOW to run the conflicting applications.
There is no good solution to this problem. You should inform your boss that a second server is required.

questions.explanation: Hyper-V allows Windows Server to host multiple virtual machines on a single physical server, ensuring OS and application isolation so that applications do not conflict with each other.
questions.answerText: a. Install Windows Server 2016 with Hyper-V and create three VMs, each running Windows Server 2016.

questions.prompt: Which of the following best describes a virtual private network (VPN)?

choices.text: runs only in a virtual machine

questions.explanation: A virtual private network offers authentication and encryption to securely transfer sensitive data over non-secure networks such as the Internet or an enterprise network.

questions.prompt: What version of Windows Server should you use if you want to deploy a hyper-converged infrastructure?
questions.explanation: Windows Server 2019 was specifically built to focus on hyper-converged infrastructures (HCI), security, and hybrid cloud datacenters.

questions.prompt: Which line of CPUs is a RISC processor?
questions.explanation: Advanced RISC Machines (ARM) processors are built on a Reduced Instruction Set Computing (RISC) architecture.

questions.prompt: What program takes human-readable instructions such as load and store and turns them into opcodes?
questions.explanation: An assembler translates human-readable assembly instructions (such as load, add, and stor) into numeric opcodes that the CPU can read and execute.

questions.prompt: If you are developing a bootloader for a CPU, what do you need to know about the CPU to ensure that your bootloader code will be executed when the CPU is powered on?
questions.explanation: When power is applied, a CPU begins reading data from a memory address known as the reset vector, which points to the location of the bootloader.

questions.prompt: What type of computer program takes a high-level language and turns it into assembly code?
questions.explanation: A compiler translates high-level programming languages (such as C++ or Java) into the assembly code that is ultimately executed by the CPU.

questions.prompt: A CPU with an external clock speed of 2 GHz and a 64-bit data bus can transfer how many bytes per second?
questions.explanation: A 1 GHz CPU with a 64-bit data bus transfers 8 GB per second (1 billion ticks × 64 bits / 8 bits per byte). Therefore, a 2 GHz CPU doubles this rate to 16 GB/s.

questions.prompt: What part of a CPU holds millions or billions of transistors on a silicon wafer?
questions.explanation: CPUs are manufactured on a silicon wafer, and the resulting component that holds all the logic and transistors is called a die.

questions.prompt: Which component of the CPU is responsible for executing arithmetic and logic instructions?
questions.explanation: The arithmetic logic unit (ALU) performs the primary task of executing arithmetic operations (like addition) and logic operations (like binary AND/OR).

questions.prompt: If you had a window into a CPU's internal components, where would you look to find information about the next instruction the CPU executes?
questions.explanation: The program counter is a specific register on the CPU that stores the memory address of the next instruction the processor needs to execute.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is true about RISC CPUs versus CISC CPUs? (Choose all that apply.)

choices.text: They require a more complex compiler.

questions.explanation: RISC chips lack microcode, allowing more physical space for registers. They also require a more complex compiler because their high-level code must be broken down into more assembly steps than CISC processors require.
questions.answerText: b. They require a more complex compiler., c. They have more registers.

questions.prompt: Where must data be placed on a CPU before it can use the data for arithmetic instructions?
questions.explanation: A register acts as a temporary holding location on the CPU where data is stored directly before the CPU processes it.

questions.prompt: Which cache level provides the fastest access to its data?
questions.explanation: Level 1 (L1) cache is built directly into the processor core and operates at the fastest speeds, generally matching the internal clock speed of the CPU.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is true about CISC CPUs?

choices.text: They have a simple instruction set.
They require a more complex compiler.

questions.explanation: CISC instructions are highly complex and perform multiple operations per instruction, requiring a small built-in program called microcode to interpret and execute them.

questions.prompt: Manufacturers rate their CPU speeds based on which characteristic?

choices.text: core speed multiplied by the number of cores

questions.explanation: The internal clock speed—the speed at which a CPU executes an instruction internally—is the most frequently used indicator of processor speed.

questions.prompt: Which component of a computer carries data between the CPU and memory?
questions.explanation: A bus acts as the internal communication pathway that carries data, instructions, and memory addresses between the central processing unit (CPU) and the system's memory.

questions.prompt: The list of commands a CPU can execute is referred to as which of the following?
questions.explanation: The instruction set refers directly to the specific list of machine code commands and operations supported by a given CPU architecture.

questions.prompt: In what way is a RISC processor sometimes more efficient than a CISC processor?

choices.text: It takes more instructions to complete a task.
RISC processors have fewer internal registers.
RISC instructions are similar to high-level language instructions.
One instruction is executed per clock cycle.

questions.explanation: RISC CPUs use simpler instructions that uniformly take one clock cycle, making them highly efficient and well-suited for pipelining multiple instructions.
questions.answerText: d. One instruction is executed per clock cycle.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is used to keep the CPU informed of the status of resources and devices connected to the computer?
questions.explanation: The control bus transports vital status signals, read/write states, and interrupt requests between the CPU and the computer's other components.

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of microcode?

choices.text: It helps the CPU find the bootloader.
It carries out complex CPU instructions.
It translates assembly language to opcodes.
It is the location pointed to by the reset vector.

questions.explanation: Microcode serves as an intermediary program inside CISC chips, interpreting and carrying out the processor's highly complex commands.
questions.answerText: b. It carries out complex CPU instructions.

questions.prompt: Which feature of a CPU allows it to execute a set of four instructions three times in fewer than twelve clock cycles?
questions.explanation: Pipelining allows a CPU to start processing subsequent instructions before the first one finishes, completing overlapping tasks across fewer clock cycles.

questions.prompt: Which part of a CPU carries signals to indicate where data should be read from or written to in the system's memory?
questions.explanation: The address bus is a dedicated internal communications pathway that specifies the exact source or target addresses for memory reads and writes.

questions.prompt: You recently installed a hard disk in a computer with UEFI firmware. The MBR-partitioned hard disk already has Windows 10 v1903 installed. When you power up the computer, it won't boot. What is a likely reason for this?

choices.text: UEFI computers only work with SSDs.
Windows 10 can't be installed on MBR disks.
UEFI systems boot from GPT-partitioned disks.
UEFI systems only work with Windows Server 2019 systems.

questions.explanation: To successfully boot an operating system, GPT disks are typically paired with UEFI firmware systems. Conversely, MBR disks are intended for systems utilizing traditional BIOS firmware.
questions.answerText: c. UEFI systems boot from GPT-partitioned disks.

questions.prompt: In which file system would you find the Master File Table?
questions.explanation: Instead of relying on a standard file allocation table and directory structure, NTFS tracks clusters and file records using a Master File Table (MFT).

questions.prompt: In what file system(s) would you find inodes? (Choose all that apply.)
questions.explanation: Native Linux file systems, such as the UNIX file system (ufs) and the extended file system (ext, which includes versions like ext3), physically store information on the disk using a structure built on information nodes, or "inodes". Each file is identified by an inode number, which contains the file's general information and logical block pointers. In contrast, FAT16 and NTFS are Windows file systems that use different structures, such as a file allocation table or the Master File Table (MFT), rather than inodes.

questions.prompt: On a Windows-based system, which of the following are contained in the Master Boot Record? (Choose all that apply.)

choices.text: partition table with up to four entries

questions.explanation: The Master Boot Record (MBR) primarily contains the bootstrap code necessary to locate the OS, a partition table supporting up to four entries, an optional disk signature and timestamp, and a boot signature marking the MBR's end.
questions.answerText: a. boot signature, b. bootstrap code, d. partition table with up to four entries

questions.prompt: While you are using some files on a workstation running Linux, you determine that a few of the files seem to be corrupted. What should you do?

choices.text: Close all files and applications and run fsck.
Start DiskScan to check for file links.
Reformat your disk using the format command.
Use the Disk Check utility, which can be run at any time.

questions.explanation: The file system checker (fsck) is a Linux utility used to verify the integrity of file systems and fix corruption issues, such as unlinked inodes. It should only be run after files and applications are safely closed to prevent further damage.
questions.answerText: a. Close all files and applications and run fsck.

questions.prompt: You are about to make many changes to your macOS files and folder. You are concerned that you might make a mistake, and you want to be able to roll back your changes if something goes wrong. What should you do?

choices.text: Open PowerShell and run the Make-ShadowCopies cmdlet.
In Disk Utility, click the volume you are going to change and select Mirror.
Open Disk Management, right-click the disk, and click Backup.
Open a terminal window and run tmutil snapshot.

questions.explanation: On macOS, Apple File System (APFS) supports snapshots that allow the system to be rolled back to a previous point in time. Users can manually generate a snapshot by running the tmutil snapshot command in the terminal.
questions.answerText: d. Open a terminal window and run tmutil snapshot.

questions.prompt: You need to create a new folder in a Linux system and you choose to do so from a terminal window. Which of the following commands enables you to create a folder?
questions.explanation: The mkdir command is the standard Linux terminal command explicitly used to create a new directory (folder).

questions.prompt: Which of the following holds information about the layout of blocks and sectors in the Linux file system?
questions.explanation: In a Linux environment, the superblock identifies the file system itself and stores critical structural data, including the layout of blocks, sectors, and cylinder groups.

questions.prompt: Your assistant has documentation that shows how to modify a device file in Linux, but the documentation does not mention which folder to find the file in. Which folder should you suggest?
questions.explanation: In Linux file systems, special device files that represent hardware like disk partitions or serial ports are typically stored in the /dev (or /devices) folder.

questions.prompt: You have created a two-terabyte volume and you are going to format it with NTFS. You are in a hurry and you don't want the formatting process to do a detailed check of the disk. What option can you use with the format command?
questions.explanation: Appending the /q (quick format) switch tells the format utility to skip the detailed disk check for bad locations. This simply writes a new root folder and file allocation table, speeding up the overall process.

questions.prompt: On a Windows 10 computer, you have installed a new 500 GB hard disk. Using the diskpart command-line tool, you begin creating 100 GB primary partitions for storing various types of files. When you attempt to create the fifth partition, you find that you can't. Why?

choices.text: The disk is a basic disk with MBR partitioning.
Windows 10 supports a maximum of four partitions on all disks.
You need to use the ReFS file system.
You formatted the partitions with FAT16, which only allows a 400 GB disk.

questions.explanation: The Master Boot Record (MBR) partitioning scheme is structurally limited to a maximum of four primary partition entries on a single disk.
questions.answerText: a. The disk is a basic disk with MBR partitioning.

questions.prompt: You want to make access to files easier for your users. Currently, files are stored on several NTFS volumes such as the C:, D:, and E: drives. You want users to be able to access all files by specifying only the C: drive so they don't have to remember which drive letter to use. For example, if the accounting files are stored on the D: drive, users should be able to access them using C:\accounting. What can you do?

choices.text: Create hard links to the files on the other drives.
Create aliases for the files on the D: and E: drives.

questions.explanation: Volume mount points allow a system administrator to map the root of a disk volume directly into an empty folder on an existing NTFS volume. This eliminates the need for separate drive letters.

questions.prompt: In Windows 10, how would you specify a file named payroll.xls located in a folder named accounting on a drive assigned the letter D?
questions.explanation: Standard Windows file path syntax dictates starting with the drive letter and a colon, followed by backslashes (\) separating the subsequent directories and the filename.

questions.prompt: What file system is used on a hard disk in a computer running Mac OS X 10.10 Yosemite?
questions.explanation: Mac OS Extended (also known as HFS+) is the standard file system used on macOS 10.12 Sierra and all earlier versions, which includes OS X 10.10 Yosemite.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is a process that marks the location of tracks and sectors on a disk?
questions.explanation: A low-level format is the initial factory process that permanently marks the layout of concentric disk tracks and divided sectors on the physical disk surface.

questions.prompt: You are installing a file-sharing application on a Windows Server 2016 server in which the volumes are managed by Storage Spaces and fault tolerance is a major consideration. Which file system should you use?
questions.explanation: Resilient File System (ReFS) is specifically engineered for large file-sharing operations where Storage Spaces manages the volumes. ReFS provides extreme fault tolerance by automatically repairing minor disk failures caused by corruption.

questions.prompt: You were given a removable 64 GB flash drive, and you will be using it to transfer files between several Windows systems and macOS computers. You want to format it to erase any existing data. What format should you select?
questions.explanation: The exFAT file system is highly compatible with both Windows and macOS platforms and is strictly required by Windows to format partitions larger than 32 GB (the maximum standard for FAT32).

questions.prompt: You have installed a second disk in your Windows 10 computer. The disk has only been low-level formatted. What is the first thing that must occur before you can begin using the disk to store files?

choices.text: Use Disk Scrub to ensure there are no bad spots on the disk.
Initialize the disk with the root folder.

questions.explanation: Once a disk possesses a low-level format, it must be partitioned to explicitly reserve storage boundaries for a file system before it can undergo high-level formatting.

questions.prompt: You overhear a colleague discussing file systems, and she mentions containers and Space Sharing. What file system is she discussing?
questions.explanation: The Apple File System (APFS) organizes reserved drive space into containers. The Space Sharing feature allows multiple volumes inside that container to dynamically expand and share the available space as needed.

questions.prompt: Users on your organization's Windows Server 2016 server are beginning to take up excessive disk space on the NTFS volumes. You have plenty of disk space now, but you're concerned about this situation in the future. What can you do?

choices.text: Enforce stronger security so it is harder for users to write files to their home directories.
Encrypt portions of the users' home directories so they can only be used by the administrator account.
Use bigger blocks for the partition.

questions.explanation: Establishing disk quotas allows system administrators to monitor and strictly enforce a hard limit on the amount of physical disk space individual user files can occupy on an NTFS volume.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is not a typical Windows Server postinstallation task?
questions.explanation: Choosing to install the Server Core role is a core configuration choice made during the initial setup, not a task performed after the operating system is installed. Typical postinstallation tasks include activating the server, setting the time zone, configuring IP parameters, and assigning a computer name.
questions.answerText: a. Installing the Server Core role

questions.prompt: Which of the following is not a valid installation option for Windows Server 2016?

choices.text: A clean installation of Windows Server 2016 Datacenter
An upgrade from Windows Server 2012 R2 Server Core to Windows Server 2016 Desktop Experience
An upgrade from Windows Server 2016 Standard to Windows Server 2019 Datacenter
A clean installation of Windows Server 2016 Server Core

questions.explanation: If you are running a Server Core installation of an older operating system, you can only perform an in-place upgrade to another Server Core installation. Upgrading directly from Server Core to a Desktop Experience (GUI) installation is not supported and requires a clean installation.
questions.answerText: b. An upgrade from Windows Server 2012 R2 Server Core to Windows Server 2016 Desktop Experience

questions.prompt: What is required to install the Hyper-V server role on Windows Server?
questions.explanation: To successfully run the Hyper-V virtualization role, your CPU must support hardware virtualization extensions, which are labeled as Intel-VT on Intel processors and AMD-V on AMD processors.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is true about Windows Server 2016?

choices.text: You can upgrade from Windows Server 2008 x86.
You can upgrade from Server Core to Server with a GUI.
You can't upgrade to a different language.

questions.explanation: Language migration is strictly unsupported when upgrading Windows Server. Both the old server version and the new destination server must run the exact same language package.
questions.answerText: d. You can't upgrade to a different language.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is a task you must do during a clean installation of Windows Server?

choices.text: Choose the disk where it will be installed.
Create a new user to be the system administrator.

questions.explanation: During the initial installation screens, you must specify the storage device or disk partition where the operating system will be placed. Setting the domain and naming the server are handled post-installation, and you do not create a new administrator user because Windows Server uses the built-in Administrator account by default.
questions.answerText: b. Choose the disk where it will be installed.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is the default setting for Windows Update on Windows Server 2019 after you first turn on automatic updates?

choices.text: Inform you when updates are available but do not download updates.

questions.explanation: By default, Windows Server is set to download updates without installing them automatically. This gives IT administrators control over when to install the patches and reboot the server, ensuring that automatic restarts do not disrupt critical network services during production hours.

questions.prompt: You are running Windows Server 2008 on a 32-bit CPU. You know that support for the OS is about to end and you have been told to upgrade to Windows Server 2019. What can you do?

choices.text: Run the Windows Server Upgrade program and insert the Windows Server 2016 installation DVD.
First, upgrade to Windows Server 2008 R2, and then upgrade to Windows Server 2019.
Install Windows Server 2019 on a new computer and migrate server roles.
Back up the computer, perform a clean installation of Windows Server 2019, and then restore the data and applications.

questions.explanation: Microsoft ceased production of 32-bit server operating systems starting with Windows Server 2008 R2, meaning Windows Server 2019 is strictly 64-bit and will not run on your current 32-bit CPU. Furthermore, in-place upgrades from Windows Server 2008 to 2019 are unsupported. The only option is to perform a clean installation on new hardware and use migration tools to transfer the existing server roles.
questions.answerText: c. Install Windows Server 2019 on a new computer and migrate server roles.

questions.prompt: You have been asked to evaluate Fedora Linux for use as a client computer in the Engineering department. However, all your client computers are running Windows 10 and you don't have any spare client machines for installing Linux. You also have a departmental server that's already running Windows Server 2016 with Hyper-V. Which of the following are options for performing this evaluation that don't risk destroying data on your existing computers? (Choose all that apply.)

choices.text: Boot a Windows 10 computer, run the setup.exe program from the Linux DVD, and choose the option to run Linux in Windows.
Use any computer, boot to the DVD, and run the evaluation without installing Linux to the hard drive.
Create a virtual machine and install Linux in a VM.
Install Linux on a Windows 10 computer in the C:\Linux folder.

questions.explanation: Fedora and many other Linux distributions offer a "Live install" option, allowing you to boot from a DVD or USB and run the operating system in memory without altering the physical hard drive. Alternatively, since a Hyper-V server is available, you can safely create a virtual machine to install and evaluate the OS without affecting the host environment.
questions.answerText: b. Use any computer, boot to the DVD, and run the evaluation without installing Linux to the hard drive, AND c. Create a virtual machine and install Linux in a VM.

questions.prompt: In which of the following circumstances is server migration required when you want to upgrade to Windows Server 2019 Datacenter Desktop Experience? (Choose all that apply.)

choices.text: When you're running a Server Core installation of Windows Server 2012 R2 Datacenter
When you're running a GUI installation of Windows Server 2012 R2 Standard
When you're running a GUI installation of Windows Server 2008
When you're running a GUI installation of Windows Server 2016 Datacenter

questions.explanation: Upgrading directly from a Server Core installation to a Desktop Experience (GUI) installation is not supported; it requires a clean install and server migration. Likewise, Windows Server 2008 is too old to support a direct in-place upgrade to 2019, as upgrades are only supported from Windows Server 2012 and newer.
questions.answerText: a. When you're running a Server Core installation of Windows Server 2012 R2 Datacenter, AND c. When you're running a GUI installation of Windows Server 2008

questions.prompt: Which of the following is true about upgrading to Windows Server 2019?

choices.text: An upgrade from Windows Server 2008 edition requires a clean installation.
You can upgrade from a Chinese version to an English version.
A Server Core installation always requires a clean installation.
You can upgrade from Windows Server 2008 R2.

questions.explanation: Direct in-place upgrades to Windows Server 2019 are only supported for servers currently running Windows Server 2012, 2012 R2, or 2016. Any earlier operating systems, including Windows Server 2008, necessitate a clean installation followed by a server role migration.
questions.answerText: a. An upgrade from Windows Server 2008 edition requires a clean installation.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is true about the macOS Mojave Server add-on?

choices.text: It comes with DNS and DHCP servers.
You must install the add-on to use Time Machine Server.
It is compatible with Active Directory.
It's a free download from the App Store.

questions.explanation: The macOS Server add-on includes the Open Directory feature, which allows administrators to seamlessly integrate macOS Server with existing directory services like Microsoft Active Directory. The other options are incorrect because the add-on costs about $20, no longer includes DNS or DHCP as of version 5.71, and Time Machine Server is now bundled directly into the base macOS rather than the add-on.
questions.answerText: c. It is compatible with Active Directory.

questions.prompt: A colleague asks you to research a CPU for a new server that will run Windows Server 2019. He explains the server roles that he intends to install and says that the CPU must support Nested Page Table. What is your colleague most likely planning to install on the server?
questions.explanation: Nested Page Table (NPT) is AMD's terminology for second-level address translation (SLAT). This specific hardware virtualization extension is a prerequisite for installing and running the Hyper-V role on Windows Server.

questions.prompt: You're trying to decide which disk technology to use on your new Windows Server 2019 installation. The server will be in heavy use around the clock every day, so high performance and reliability is a necessity. Which technology is the best choice?
questions.explanation: Serial Attached SCSI (SAS) disks are specifically engineered for continuous, round-the-clock use. They offer superior performance and reliability compared to consumer-grade technologies for high-demand enterprise servers.

questions.prompt: Under which conditions should you consider a clean installation? (Choose all that apply.)

choices.text: The installation is needed for a computer that has no OS installed.
You want to replace the current OS but maintain all your settings.
You don't want to have to reinstall applications.
You want to be able to boot to your old OS and the new OS.

questions.explanation: A clean installation is defined as installing the operating system on a new disk partition rather than overwriting an older version. This is mandatory when a computer is completely blank, and it is the necessary method when setting up a dual-boot configuration to maintain access to an old OS on one partition while running a new OS on another.
questions.answerText: a. The installation is needed for a computer that has no OS installed, AND d. You want to be able to boot to your old OS and the new OS.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is a reason for installing a new server? (Choose all that apply.)
questions.explanation: Expanding a network by adding new servers is typically done to accommodate company growth, distribute excessive processing loads, ensure fault tolerance for essential services, or isolate resource-heavy applications so they don't disrupt other operations. Adding a new network protocol is not a recognized reason for requiring an entirely new server.
questions.answerText: a. Excessive load on existing servers, b. Fault tolerance, AND d. To isolate a new application

questions.prompt: A new junior technician asks you why it takes so long to access a file on your tape backup system compared to the server's hard drive. What can you tell her is the most likely explanation for the slow access?

choices.text: The tape backup system uses FIFO chips, which are very slow.
The tape backup system is a sequential-access device.
The tape backup system uses DMA instead of PIO.
The tape backup system uses polling instead of interrupts.

questions.explanation: Tape drives are classified as sequential-access devices. This means that to access data at a specific location, the system must read sequentially through all preceding data locations first, making it significantly slower than random-access hard drives.
questions.answerText: b. The tape backup system is a sequential-access device.

questions.prompt: When a Linux application prints a document, what accepts the document and stores it in a temporary location before it is sent to the printer?
questions.explanation: When an application sends a print job in Linux, a print spooler receives the job and holds it in a temporary file called a print queue until the printer is ready to process it.

questions.prompt: Where are print jobs stored before being sent to the print device?
questions.explanation: The print spooler places print jobs into a print queue, which serves as a temporary storage location until the documents can be dispatched to the printer.

questions.prompt: When you create a device special file in Linux, in what folder should it be stored?
questions.explanation: In most Linux distributions, device special files that contain information about I/O devices are stored in the /dev directory.

questions.prompt: In Linux, which type of device special file is used to handle internal communications such as output redirection?
questions.explanation: Named pipes are a specific category of Linux device special files dedicated to handling internal system communications, such as redirecting file output to a terminal.

questions.prompt: What is the most common printing system used in contemporary Linux distributions?
questions.explanation: CUPS is the standard, modular printing system used across modern Linux distributions and Unix-like operating systems. It manages print requests, job scheduling, queues, and printer communications (often utilizing the Internet Printing Protocol, or IPP, as its underlying protocol).

questions.prompt: Which of the following is not true about I/O devices and device drivers?

choices.text: Device drivers provide communication services between the physical device and the OS.
Device drivers handle input from the keyboard and mouse.
User applications usually communicate directly with a device driver.
The control register on a device takes commands from the device driver.

questions.explanation: User applications do not communicate directly with device drivers; instead, the application sends a request to the operating system, which then forwards the request to the correct device driver.
questions.answerText: c. User applications usually communicate directly with a device driver.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is not a component of most I/O devices?
questions.explanation: Most standard I/O devices operate using an I/O controller, a control register, and one or more data registers. They do not utilize an instruction register.

questions.prompt: You are the computer support person in your small company. An employee has installed an off-brand NIC in his Windows 10 computer that he recently used with his old Windows XP computer. He is now trying to install the device driver that he downloaded from the Internet. However, Windows 10 will not install the driver. You bring a NIC that you have installed in many other Windows 10 computers, and the driver installs successfully. What is a likely reason why Windows 10 would not allow the driver for the off-brand NIC to be installed?
questions.explanation: Starting with Windows 7, Microsoft requires a digital signature on drivers to verify their authenticity and integrity. Windows 10 will block the installation of unsigned drivers by default, which is common with older or off-brand hardware.

questions.prompt: After you install a new sound card and its related device drivers, your monitor frequently pauses or stops working. You often have to reboot the system, but the problem persists. Which of the following is most likely to be the problem?

choices.text: You need a new display adapter.
There is an I/O address range conflict.
You need to update the display driver.

questions.explanation: When two or more devices are assigned overlapping system resources, such as the same IRQ line or I/O address range, the conflicting devices can become unstable or stop working entirely.
questions.answerText: c. There is an I/O address range conflict.

questions.prompt: You support the Windows 10 computers in your organization. A new network interface driver has been issued to plug a security hole. Which tool would you use to quickly install this driver update?
questions.explanation: Device Manager is the standard Windows utility used to install new device drivers, update existing ones, or roll back drivers to previous versions.

questions.prompt: Which command in Linux enables you to create a device special file?
questions.explanation: The mknod command is used in Linux terminal environments (alongside superuser permissions) to manually create device special files for new hardware.

questions.prompt: You are writing a device driver for an audio device connected to your computer. Your code needs to determine if the device is busy or ready to accept a new command. How can the driver determine this?
questions.explanation: The status register on a device is used to signal its current state to the device driver, indicating whether the hardware is ready to accept a command, currently busy, or if an interrupt has occurred.

questions.prompt: What component of a device does a device driver access if data should be output by the device?
questions.explanation: The data register is the specific storage location where the device driver writes the data that the device is intended to output, and where it reads the data that the device inputs.

questions.prompt: You have been troubleshooting a performance issue with a system that has just had a new block device installed along with its driver. The driver code was written by a new software development intern. When the device is accessed, you notice high CPU utilization. Which of the following is the most likely solution to the problem?

choices.text: Add a FIFO chip to the device.
Change the device to use character streaming.
Use DMA to perform data transfers.
Use programmed I/O to communicate with the device registers.

questions.explanation: Using Programmed I/O (PIO) for high-speed block devices creates high CPU overhead because the CPU must process every byte. Implementing direct memory access (DMA) allows a dedicated DMA controller to handle large data transfers, freeing the CPU to execute other tasks and reducing utilization spikes.
questions.answerText: c. Use DMA to perform data transfers.

questions.prompt: In UNIX and Linux, which of the following is true about device drivers?

choices.text: They must be written in C or Pascal.
They must never be kernel modules.

questions.explanation: Linux device drivers operate within the kernel and can exist either as kernel modules linked directly into the kernel code or as loadable modules that are loaded dynamically when the operating system starts.
questions.answerText: b. They can be loadable modules.

questions.prompt: You need to check a printer parameter for a Linux printer. In what directory should you look for information about the printer configuration?
questions.explanation: The Common UNIX Printing System (CUPS) is the standard printing system for most Linux distributions, and its primary configuration files, including printer parameters, are housed in the /etc/cups directory.

questions.prompt: Which component might you include in a device you are designing if the device needs to accept bursts of data that can be held until the CPU is ready for it?
questions.explanation: A first-in first-out (FIFO) chip supplements standard data registers by storing multiple bytes or words of incoming or outgoing data in sequential order. This allows the device controller to handle temporary bursts of data and hold them until the CPU is ready to process them.

questions.prompt: What communicates between the OS and computer devices?
questions.explanation: Device drivers act as the fundamental software bridge, providing communication services that allow the operating system and applications to interact with physical hardware devices.

questions.prompt: In which type of I/O does the CPU execute special instructions to read and write the I/O ports?
questions.explanation: Port-mapped I/O uses dedicated memory addresses separated from the main RAM. It requires the CPU to execute special I/O instructions to interact with device registers, triggering the I/O bus to select the proper hardware.

questions.prompt: What type of interface are you likely to find that externally connects a DAS device to the server that uses it?
questions.explanation: Direct-attached storage (DAS) devices that have their own enclosures connect to servers using external bus interfaces. Common external interfaces for DAS include eSATA, SCSI, USB, FireWire, and Fibre Channel.

questions.prompt: On your Windows server, you're planning to install a new database application that uses an enormous amount of disk space. You need this application to be highly available, so you need a disk system with the capability to auto-correct from disk errors and data corruption. You also want a flexible storage solution that makes it easy to add space and supports deduplication. Which of the following is the best option?
questions.explanation: Storage Spaces is a Windows model that provisions virtual storage flexibly and includes a data deduplication feature to reduce space consumption. The Resilient File System (ReFS) is highly resilient and currently supports massive volume sizes of up to 35 petabytes (PB).
questions.answerText: c. ReFS format and Storage Spaces

questions.prompt: Which disk interface technology transfers data over a parallel bus?
questions.explanation: The small computer system interface (SCSI) is a parallel drive technology historically used in enterprise-class servers. It operates on a parallel bus similar to older parallel ATA (PATA) technology.

questions.prompt: You have a server with Windows Server 2016 installed on Disk 0, a basic disk. You use the server to store users' documents. You have two more disks that you can install in the server. What should you do if you want to provide fault tolerance for users' documents?

choices.text: Convert Disk 0 to dynamic. Create a striped volume using Disk 0, Disk 1, and Disk 2.
Create a RAID 1 volume from Disk 1 and Disk 2.
Convert the new disks to GPT. Create a spanned volume using Disk 1 and Disk 2.
Create a RAID 5 volume from Disk 0, Disk 1, and Disk 2.

questions.explanation: A RAID 1 (mirrored) volume provides fault tolerance by duplicating data across two separate disks. Because Disk 0 holds the operating system, Disk 1 and Disk 2 should be utilized independently to create a secure, fault-tolerant mirror for user documents.
questions.answerText: b. Create a RAID 1 volume from Disk 1 and Disk 2.

questions.prompt: What is created automatically when you install Windows Server 2019 on a system with a disk drive that has never had an OS installed on it before?
questions.explanation: In Windows 2008 and later versions, the system volume is created automatically during the initial OS installation on a new drive. This volume holds the boot files the computer needs to locate and load the operating system.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is true about an SSD?
questions.explanation: A solid-state drive (SSD) operates using flash memory chips. Because it lacks magnetic platters and read/write heads, an SSD contains no moving mechanical parts.
questions.answerText: b. It has no moving parts.

questions.prompt: You need a disk system that provides the best performance for a new application that frequently reads and writes data to the disk. You aren't concerned about disk fault tolerance because the data will be backed up each day; performance is the main concern. What type of volume arrangement should you use?
questions.explanation: A RAID 0 (striped) volume distributes data across multiple disks, which provides a significant read and write performance advantage over simple or spanned volumes. It does not offer fault tolerance, making it ideal for scenarios prioritizing speed.

questions.prompt: What does a storage area network use to identify units of storage?
questions.explanation: A storage area network (SAN) uses a logical unit number (LUN) as a reference point to identify a unit of storage. A LUN simplifies management for the server by referencing a portion of a disk, a single disk, or an entire disk array.

questions.prompt: Which disk interface technology is specific to SSDs and uses the PCIe bus?
questions.explanation: Non-volatile memory express (NVMe) is a storage interface specifically designed to connect SSDs directly to the PCIe bus. Bypassing intermediate controllers allows NVMe to achieve speeds vastly superior to SATA SSDs.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is true about a page file?

choices.text: It should be stored on a separate disk from the Windows folder.
It's usually stored in fast random access memory.
Windows stores frequently accessed drivers in it.
It is usually smaller than 50 MB.

questions.explanation: The Windows page file (pagefile.sys) acts as virtual memory to supplement physical RAM. Because the system accesses virtual memory frequently, it should ideally be stored on its own dedicated physical disk to optimize overall performance.
questions.answerText: a. It should be stored on a separate disk from the Windows folder.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is true about GPT disks?

choices.text: They support a maximum volume size of 2 TB.
GPT is the default option when initializing a disk in Disk Management.
They use CRC protection for the partition table.
You can't convert a GPT disk to MBR.

questions.explanation: The GUID Partitioning Table (GPT) method offers enhanced reliability over older partitioning methods by maintaining partition table replication. Additionally, GPT disks utilize cyclic redundancy check (CRC) protection to safeguard the partition table against corruption.
questions.answerText: c. They use CRC protection for the partition table.

questions.prompt: What type of volumes or partitions can be created on a basic disk? (Choose all that apply.)
questions.explanation: A basic disk only accommodates simple volumes, which are designated as primary partitions. If a user creates a fourth partition on a basic disk, it is categorized as an extended partition.
questions.answerText: c. extended partition; d. simple volume

questions.prompt: Which of the following is an example of the types of information that a computer stores? (Choose all that apply.)
questions.explanation: Computers require disk space to store operating system files, user applications, user documents, virtual memory, log files, virtual machines, and database storage. Working memory refers to volatile RAM rather than long-term storage data.
questions.answerText: a. virtual memory; b. log files; d. documents

questions.prompt: You want shared network storage that's easy to set up and geared toward file sharing with several file-sharing protocols. What should you consider buying?
questions.explanation: Network-attached storage (NAS) is a dedicated appliance with a built-in OS specifically tailored to make file sharing easy to configure. NAS supports standard network file-sharing protocols like SMB, NFS, and FTP.

questions.prompt: You have installed a new disk and created a volume on it. What should you do before you can store files on it?
questions.explanation: A volume cannot be utilized by an operating system until it is formatted. Formatting prepares the disk with a file system used to logically organize and store files.

questions.prompt: Which of the following commands can verify a new partition you have configured in Linux? (Choose all that apply.)
questions.explanation: In Linux systems, the sfdisk command-line utility (alongside cfdisk) allows administrators to list partition information, repartition a disk, and verify partitions.

questions.prompt: You are ordering eight new desktop computers for your small business. Which of the following hard drive technologies is likely to be used in the new computers?
questions.explanation: Serial ATA (SATA) drives are inexpensive, fast, and highly reliable. These characteristics make SATA drives the standard fit for typical client desktop computers and lower-end servers.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is an example of non-volatile storage? (Choose all that apply.)
questions.explanation: Non-volatile storage retains saved data permanently even without an active power source. Common non-volatile storage mediums include hard disk drives, magnetic tape, flash drives, and solid-state drives (SSDs).

questions.prompt: You have four servers that need access to shared disk storage because you're configuring them in a cluster. Which storage solution should you consider for this application?
questions.explanation: A storage area network (SAN) uses high-speed networking to provide large capacities of shared disk storage. SANs are explicitly designed for server clusters so that all cluster members share access to the same storage for load balancing and fault tolerance.

questions.prompt: You come across a file with a .vhdx extension on your Windows 10 computer's hard disk. What should you do to see this file's contents?

choices.text: Right-click the file and click Open.
Burn the file to a DVD.

questions.explanation: A file with a .vhdx extension is a virtual hard disk. Windows 10 allows you to view its contents by right-clicking the file and selecting Mount, which treats the file as a regular physical volume.

questions.prompt: Which of the following are reasons to use bare-metal virtualization? (Choose all that apply.)
questions.explanation: Server consolidation using bare-metal virtualization provides the direct benefits of allowing organizations to retire old or unreliable hardware, reclaim physical rack or floor space, and drastically reduce datacenter cooling and power requirements.
questions.answerText: a. retiring old hardware, c. reducing cooling, d. reclaiming floor space

questions.prompt: You have two Hyper-V hosts, each running three VMs. You want to be able to periodically perform maintenance operations on the hosts without losing the services provided by the VMs. You also want to maintain VM operation in the event of a host failure. You don't have shared storage between the hosts. What is the best way to accomplish this?
questions.explanation: VM replication automatically copies the primary VM and its virtual hard disks to a replica server and updates it periodically. Because it does not require shared storage, this allows administrators to manually failover to the replica VM during a host failure or planned maintenance.

questions.prompt: Which virtualization technology virtualizes an application environment but shares parts of the host OS?
questions.explanation: A container isolates an application within a virtualized software environment while sharing critical system components, such as the kernel, runtime libraries, and the host hardware, directly with the host OS.

questions.prompt: Which of the following can best be described as developing applications by using a service provider's development tools and infrastructure?
questions.explanation: A hosted platform, more commonly known as Platform as a Service (PaaS), is a cloud computing model in which a customer uses the service provider's tools and hardware infrastructure to develop and deploy their own applications.

questions.prompt: Which feature of some virtualization products allows you to deploy VMs and storage as needed and has uses in cloud computing?
questions.explanation: Dynamic provisioning is an advanced VM management feature that dynamically deploys VMs and storage to meet fluctuating application requirements. It serves as a foundational component for clustered and cloud computing architectures.

questions.prompt: You have been assigned the task of consolidating servers in your datacenter so you can reduce the number of physical servers and make better use of the processing power of some of the newer rackmount servers your company has purchased. What technology should you use to accomplish this?
questions.explanation: Bare-metal virtualization uses a Type 1 hypervisor installed directly onto the hardware, making it the industry standard for production server consolidation and resource optimization in datacenters.

questions.prompt: If you want your virtual machine to have direct access to the physical network, which virtual network option should you configure in VMware Workstation?
questions.explanation: The bridged networking option directly connects the VM's virtual network interface to the host’s physical Network Interface Card (NIC). This allows the VM to receive its own IP address and function as an independent computer on the physical network.

questions.prompt: You are using vSphere to virtualize some of your production servers. You have created a new virtual switch to provide network connectivity for the VMs. After you create the virtual switch, you still cannot connect the VMs to it. What do you need to do?
questions.explanation: In VMware vSphere, creating a virtual switch is only the first step; one or more port groups must be created and configured on the switch to actually route management traffic or VM traffic.

questions.prompt: Which virtualization product uses a Web browser to manage the host and VMs?
questions.explanation: Once initial text-based configuration is completed on the server, VMware vSphere's remote configuration and VM administration are handled entirely through the vSphere Web Client, which is accessible via any Web browser.

questions.prompt: Which Hyper-V virtual switch configuration is isolated from the host computer?
questions.explanation: A private virtual switch securely isolates virtual machines by only allowing communication between the VMs connected to it. It completely prevents network access to the host computer and the external physical network.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is true about bare-metal virtualization?

choices.text: It supports a wider variety of guest OSs than hosted virtualization.
It uses the host OS to access hardware.
VMware Workstation Player is an example.

questions.explanation: Bare-metal virtualization is defined by its use of a type 1 hypervisor. Instead of running on top of a general-purpose host OS, the virtualization software is installed and runs directly on the host computer's hardware.
questions.answerText: c. It uses a type 1 hypervisor.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is the virtual environment that emulates a physical computer's hardware and BIOS?
questions.explanation: A virtual machine (VM) is the fundamental software environment created by a hypervisor to simulate the physical components, memory, and BIOS required to run a guest operating system.

questions.prompt: Which virtual network configuration shares an IP address with the host computer?
questions.explanation: Network Address Translation (NAT) allows the virtual machine to share the host computer's IP address. The host computer acts as a router, translating internal addresses for incoming and outgoing network packets to keep the VM hidden from the broader network.

questions.prompt: In which cloud computing model does Google Apps best fit?
questions.explanation: Google Apps falls under Software as a Service (SaaS), which delivers hosted, on-demand applications to customers over the Internet so they do not have to install or manage the software locally.

questions.prompt: What can be defined as software that creates and monitors the virtual hardware environment?
questions.explanation: The hypervisor, also known as a virtual machine monitor (VMM), is the core virtualization software responsible for creating, scheduling, and monitoring the virtual hardware environment so multiple VMs can safely share a single host's physical resources.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is a partial copy of a VM that contains changes made since the VM was created?
questions.explanation: A snapshot (referred to as a checkpoint in Hyper-V) captures the exact state and any changes made to a VM since its creation or since a previous snapshot. It is primarily used to easily restore a VM to an earlier working state.

questions.prompt: Which feature provided by some virtualization products allows you to move a VM to a new host computer while the VM is running?
questions.explanation: Live migration is an enterprise feature that actively shifts running VMs between physical hardware hosts without interrupting service or incurring downtime, making it essential for reliability and dynamic performance tuning.

questions.prompt: Which OSI model layer takes a large chunk of data from the Application layer and breaks it into smaller segments?
questions.explanation: The Transport layer (Layer 4) is responsible for segmentation, which involves breaking large streams of application data into smaller, manageable segments for reliable transmission across the network.

questions.prompt: Which of the following best describes a client?

choices.text: A computer's primary role in the network is to give other computers access to network resources and services.
A computer's primary role in the network is to run user applications and access network resources.
It's the software that responds to requests for network resources.
The OS installed on a computer is designed mainly to share network resources.

questions.explanation: In a client-server architecture, the client is the end-user machine that requests and consumes services, files, or resources hosted by a central server.
questions.answerText: B. A computer's primary role in the network is to run user applications and access network resources.

questions.prompt: You work for a small company with four users who need to share information on their computers. The budget is tight, so the network must be as inexpensive as possible. What type of network should you install?
questions.explanation: Peer-to-peer (P2P) networks do not require expensive dedicated servers. Because each computer can directly share resources with others, it is the most cost-effective solution for a very small group.

questions.prompt: You're the network administrator for a company that has just expanded from one floor to two floors of a large building, and the number of workstations you need has doubled from 50 to 100. You're concerned that network performance will suffer if you add computers to the existing LAN. In addition, new users will be working in a separate business unit, and there are reasons to logically separate the two groups of computers. What type of network should you configure?
questions.explanation: An internetwork is created when multiple local area networks (LANs) are connected via routers. This logically separates the departments, reduces broadcast traffic, and maintains network performance.

questions.prompt: Which of the following accurately describes the .edu part of the FQDN www.yc.edu?
questions.explanation: In a Fully Qualified Domain Name (FQDN), the suffix (such as .edu, .com, or .org) represents the highest level in the hierarchical Domain Name System (DNS) structure, known as the top-level domain (TLD).

questions.prompt: Where does a DNS server look when it can't resolve a query from its zone records or cache?
questions.explanation: If a local DNS server does not have the IP address cached or in its local zone, it uses root hints to locate the authoritative root DNS servers on the Internet to begin the resolution process.

questions.prompt: Which protocol can configure a computer's IP address and subnet mask automatically?
questions.explanation: The Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol (DHCP) automatically assigns IP addresses, subnet masks, default gateways, and other network configurations to client devices.

questions.prompt: Which of the following characteristics is associated with a peer-to-peer network? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: Without a central server, peer-to-peer networks rely on individual users to manage their own shared files and security, making the storage decentralized and the overall network much cheaper to implement.
questions.answerText: A. decentralized data storage, B. inexpensive, C. user-managed resources

questions.prompt: In network communication, what address is used to deliver a frame to the correct computer on the network? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: Network switches operate at Layer 2 and use the physical Media Access Control (MAC) address burned into a computer's network interface card to deliver data frames on a local segment.

questions.prompt: What's the term for each grouping of 8 bits in an IP address?
questions.explanation: An IPv4 address consists of 32 bits divided into four sections of 8 bits each. Because 8 bits make a byte, these sections are officially referred to as octets.

questions.prompt: TCP/IP is an example of which of the following?
questions.explanation: Transmission Control Protocol/Internet Protocol (TCP/IP) is the foundational suite of network protocols that dictates how data is packaged, addressed, and routed across the Internet.

questions.prompt: What is the unit of information that contains MAC addresses and an error checking code that's processed by the network interface layer?
questions.explanation: At the Data Link layer (or TCP/IP Network Access layer), a packet is encapsulated into a frame, which adds the source and destination MAC addresses along with a Frame Check Sequence (FCS) for error detection.

questions.prompt: What component of a DHCP server uses the client MAC address to ensure that the client is leased the same address each time it requests an IP address?
questions.explanation: A DHCP reservation permanently ties a specific IP address to a specific device's MAC address, ensuring that the device always receives the same IP upon renewal.

questions.prompt: What type of DNS resource record is an alias for another record?
questions.explanation: A Canonical Name (CNAME) record maps an alias name to a true (canonical) domain name, allowing multiple domain names to resolve to the same underlying A-record.

questions.prompt: Which of the following IPv6 features is an enhancement to IPv4? (Choose two.)

choices.text: works at the Internetwork and Transport layers

questions.explanation: IPv6 upgrades IPv4 by utilizing 128-bit addresses (vastly increasing the address space) and natively integrating IPsec, ensuring that network security is a built-in feature rather than an add-on.
questions.answerText: A. larger address space, C. built-in security

questions.prompt: What does TCP/IP use to look up a computer's IP address when its name is known?
questions.explanation: The Domain Name System (DNS) acts as the phonebook of the Internet, translating human-readable hostnames (like www.google.com) into numerical IP addresses.

questions.prompt: What does the Transport layer use to identify source and destination Application layer protocols?
questions.explanation: The Transport layer assigns logical port numbers (such as Port 80 for HTTP or Port 443 for HTTPS) to track and route traffic to the correct application or service on the host machine.

questions.prompt: What type of message is used to determine whether a computer is listening on the network?
questions.explanation: The ping command sends Internet Control Message Protocol (ICMP) echo request packets to a destination computer to verify whether it is online, reachable, and responding.

questions.prompt: When a Windows computer is configured to use DHCP but no DHCP server is available, what type of address is configured automatically for it?
questions.explanation: Automatic Private IP Addressing (APIPA) is a Windows feature that automatically assigns a link-local IP address (in the 169.254.x.x range) so that devices on the same local subnet can still communicate if the DHCP server fails.

questions.prompt: You have installed Windows Server 2016 on a new server and want to centralize user logons and security policies. What type of software should you install and configure on this server?
questions.explanation: Directory services, such as Active Directory Domain Services (AD DS) in Windows, are used to centrally manage and authenticate user accounts, groups, and security policies across a network.

questions.prompt: The subnet mask of an IP address does which of the following?

choices.text: provides encryption in a TCP/IP network
defines network and host portions of an IP address
allows users to use a computer's name rather than its address

questions.explanation: A subnet mask acts as a filter that the computer uses to determine exactly which part of an IP address represents the overarching network and which part represents the specific host device.
questions.answerText: B. defines network and host portions of an IP address

questions.prompt: If a protocol is routable, at which TCP/IP layer does it operate?
questions.explanation: Routing occurs at the Internetwork layer (equivalent to the OSI Network layer), as this is where IP addressing handles path determination across different networks.

questions.prompt: What Application layer protocol is used for sending email over the Internet?
questions.explanation: The Simple Mail Transfer Protocol (SMTP) is the standard application protocol used for transmitting outgoing email messages from a client to a server or between servers.

questions.prompt: Which OSI layer determines the route a packet takes from sender to receiver?
questions.explanation: Layer 3 is the Network layer of the OSI model. It uses logical IP addresses and routing protocols to determine the most efficient path for a packet to reach its destination.

questions.prompt: An IPv6 address is made up of how many bits?
