questions.explanation: While IPv4 uses 32 bits, IPv6 uses a 128-bit hexadecimal addressing format to accommodate an exponentially larger number of unique IP addresses globally.

questions.prompt: What file can you print to the screen on a Linux system that contains the user accounts on that system?
questions.explanation: In Linux, the /etc/passwd file stores essential local user account information, including usernames, user IDs, group IDs, and home directory paths.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is the default protocol Windows uses to share folders?
questions.explanation: Server Message Block (SMB) is Microsoft's native network protocol for providing shared access to files, directories, and printers across a network.

questions.prompt: Which component of a file sharing client determines whether the resource is local or remote?
questions.explanation: A network redirector operates at the operating system level to intercept I/O requests and direct them either to the local storage or across the network, depending on where the requested resource resides.

questions.prompt: What is a storage location for pending print jobs?
questions.explanation: A print queue (or spool) is a temporary storage area in memory or on disk where print jobs wait in line until the printer is ready to process them.

questions.prompt: Which of the following defines the types of actions a user can perform on a system?
questions.explanation: While authentication verifies who the user is, authorization determines what the user is allowed to do (their rights and privileges) after successfully logging in.

questions.prompt: Which of the following correctly specifies a file named salaries.xls in a shared folder named Budget on a server named Accounting when accessing the file remotely from a Windows computer?
questions.explanation: Windows environments use the Universal Naming Convention (UNC) for network paths, which is always formatted using backslashes as \\ServerName\ShareName\FileName.

questions.prompt: What file can you edit on a Linux system to configure shared folders using Samba?
questions.explanation: The Samba suite, which allows Linux to interface with Windows SMB shares, relies on the smb.conf configuration file stored in the /etc/samba/ directory.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is the native Linux/UNIX file sharing protocol?
questions.explanation: Network File System (NFS) is the standard and native protocol designed specifically for sharing directories and files between Unix and Linux-based systems.

questions.prompt: A text file that contains a list of commands is called which of the following?
questions.explanation: A batch file is a plain text script file containing a sequence of commands that the operating system's command-line interpreter executes sequentially.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is the correct syntax for mapping drive letter W to a shared folder named Accounting on the Finance server?
questions.explanation: The net use command is the standard Windows command-line utility for connecting to shared network resources, followed by the chosen drive letter and the UNC path of the share.

questions.prompt: Which of the following statements is true when discussing Windows?

choices.text: Share permissions apply when interactive access is attempted.
Share permissions apply to network access and interactive access.
File and folder permissions only apply to interactive access.
File and folder permissions apply to network access and interactive access.

questions.explanation: NTFS (file and folder) permissions apply to a resource regardless of how the user accesses it (locally or over the network). In contrast, share permissions only apply when accessed remotely over the network.
questions.answerText: D) File and folder permissions apply to network access and interactive access.

questions.prompt: Which of the following group scopes can only contain users from the domain in which the group is created?
questions.explanation: In Active Directory, a Global group is restricted to containing accounts solely from its own domain, though it can be used to assign permissions to resources in any trusted domain.

questions.prompt: Which group scope can be used to assign permissions to resources only in the domain in which the group is created?
questions.explanation: Domain Local groups can contain members from any trusted domain, but their primary restriction is that they can only be granted permissions to resources located within the domain where the group itself exists.

questions.prompt: Which special identity group contains any account (except Guest) that is currently signed in to a computer or domain with a valid username and password?
questions.explanation: The Authenticated Users group automatically includes all users possessing a valid local or Active Directory account, strictly excluding anonymous logins and Guest accounts.

questions.prompt: A user has called you to complain that he does not have access to a file. While on the phone, you add the user to the appropriate group that has permission to access the file. You ask the user to try to access the file again, but he still cannot. What should you do?

choices.text: Tell the user to log off and log on again.
Delete the user account and re-create it.
Add the user to the permission list for the file.
Shut down the server and restart it.

questions.explanation: A user's access token, which contains their group memberships and permissions, is only generated at the time of logon. They must log off and sign back in to refresh this token and apply the newly assigned group permissions.
questions.answerText: A) Tell the user to log off and log on again.

questions.prompt: Which of the following questions must be answered before determining how much security your operating systems need? (Choose two.)

choices.text: What tools are used to attack the network?
What costs are associated with security being breached?
How likely is it that a threat will actually occur?
How much data is on the network?

questions.explanation: Determining an organization's security posture requires a risk assessment. This involves calculating the potential financial or operational impact of a breach and weighing it against the probability that the specific threat will actually happen.
questions.answerText: B. What costs are associated with security being breached?; C. How likely is it that a threat will actually occur?

questions.prompt: Which of the following is a guideline for creating a security policy?

choices.text: A security policy should be enforceable.
A security policy should have different provisions depending on the user.
A security policy should be general so rules can be clarified if there is a breach.
A security policy should be encrypted so black hats can't read it.

questions.explanation: A security policy is only effective if its rules and guidelines can be practically applied, monitored, and enforced by the administration. Policies that cannot be enforced hold no functional value.
questions.answerText: A. A security policy should be enforceable.

questions.prompt: Your boss has asked that you secure communication between the server that holds personal identifying information of your clients and all other computers. Which of the following technologies can you use?
questions.explanation: IPsec (Internet Protocol Security) is a suite of protocols used to authenticate and encrypt network payloads over IP networks, securing the data as it travels in transit between the server and the clients. EFS and BitLocker only protect data at rest.

questions.prompt: Which of the following backup methods backs up any files that have changed since the last full or incremental backup?
questions.explanation: An incremental backup only captures the data that has changed since the very last backup operation (whether full or incremental) and clears the archive bit.

questions.prompt: Which of the following should be a common element in any security policy?

choices.text: network access that is limited to working hours

questions.explanation: While specific password lengths or strict working-hour access rules vary based on the organization's unique needs, endpoint malware protection is a universal baseline requirement for all IT security policies.

questions.prompt: Your organization's Windows Server 2016 server has 8 GB of RAM but has been running a little slow, so you decide to check the virtual memory configuration. You find that the paging file is located on the C: drive, where Windows is installed. The paging file is about 12 GB. Is there anything you can do to configure the paging file for optimal performance?

choices.text: Decrease the paging file size to 4 GB.
Increase the paging file size to 24 GB.

questions.explanation: Moving the paging file (virtual memory) to a separate physical disk from the operating system drive reduces I/O bottlenecking, allowing the system to read and write OS processes and paging data simultaneously.
questions.answerText: B. Move it to another disk.

questions.prompt: What is the default Windows Update configuration in Windows 10?
questions.explanation: By default, Windows 10 automatically downloads and installs system updates in the background to ensure that systems remain continuously patched against security vulnerabilities without requiring user intervention.

questions.prompt: This morning you modified five large data files in your home folder in Linux, and now you want to find and delete the files because you no longer need them. Which of the following commands can you use to list and sort files based on the time they were modified?
questions.explanation: The ls command lists directory contents, and the -t flag sorts those contents by their modification time, displaying the most recently modified files first.

questions.prompt: You have a medium-sized business of over 300 Windows 10 computers and 15 Windows Server 2016 and 2019 servers. You have found that the computers are using a lot of bandwidth every night when they check for updates on Microsoft's update servers. In addition, you have no easy way of knowing which computers are up to date with the latest security patches. What is the best way to reduce the bandwidth usage and more easily document which computers have the proper updates?

choices.text: Download updates and burn them to a DVD, and use the DVD to install the updates on each computer. The DVD will also serve as documentation.
Create a script to stagger when computers perform updates and send a list of installed updates to a server.
Configure the computers to compress the updates they receive from Microsoft.
Install Windows Server Update Services on one of your servers.

questions.explanation: Windows Server Update Services (WSUS) centralizes patch management. The server downloads the updates once from Microsoft (saving bandwidth) and distributes them locally to the 300 computers while providing a centralized dashboard for compliance reporting.
questions.answerText: D. Install Windows Server Update Services on one of your servers.

questions.prompt: Which of the following forms of authentication involves a CA to verify a computer or user's identity?
questions.explanation: A digital certificate is an electronic credential issued by a Certificate Authority (CA) that mathematically binds a public key to an entity's identity using Public Key Infrastructure (PKI).

questions.prompt: Bill Smith has just been prompted to change his password. He has a list of possible passwords he is considering. Which of the following passwords is considered the most secure?
questions.explanation: This option functions as a passphrase. It is the longest option (12 characters) and includes a mix of uppercase letters, lowercase letters, numbers, symbols, and spaces, making it highly resistant to dictionary and brute-force attacks.

questions.prompt: Which command adds a rule to the Linux netfilter firewall that prevents incoming ping packets from being processed?
questions.explanation: This command appends (-A) a rule to the INPUT chain, specifying that any incoming packet using the ICMP protocol (-p icmp, which is the protocol ping utilizes) should jump (-j) to the DROP target, effectively silently discarding it.

questions.prompt: What should you install on an operating system to prevent potentially harmful network packets from entering or leaving the OS?
questions.explanation: A host-based firewall is software installed directly on an individual operating system. It inspects, permits, or denies inbound and outbound network traffic based on configured security rules.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is an element of a security policy? (Choose all that apply.)
questions.explanation: A comprehensive organizational security policy acts as an umbrella document that typically includes specific sub-policies, such as authentication guidelines (how users verify their identity) and privacy policies (how data is handled and protected).
questions.answerText: A. authentication policy; B. privacy policy

questions.prompt: In Linux, you are preparing to delete the tprice user account because the user has just left the company. However, before you delete the account, you want to list all files owned by tprice so you can decide which files to keep. What command enables you to view all files owned by the tprice account?
questions.explanation: The find command searches the directory tree. Specifying / tells it to start at the root directory (searching the entire system), and -user tprice filters the results to only show files owned by that specific account.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is a Windows Defender Firewall profile? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: Windows Defender Firewall categorizes network connections into three distinct profiles to apply appropriate security rules: Domain (connected to an Active Directory domain), Private (trusted local networks), and Public (untrusted networks like coffee shops).

questions.prompt: You have a password policy that users must change their password every 90 days. You don't want them to re-use a password for at least 10 passwords. What option should you set on a Windows system to ensure that users can't re-use a recent password?
questions.explanation: The "Enforce password history" setting dictates how many previous passwords Windows remembers. Setting it to 10 forces the user to create unique passwords for their next 10 cycles before an old one can be reused.

questions.prompt: Which backup scheme requires the fewest tapes to perform a full restore?
questions.explanation: To perform a complete system restore under this scheme, you only need exactly two tapes: the most recent full backup tape and the most recent differential backup tape (since differential backups contain all changes made since the full backup).

questions.prompt: In multifactor authentication, which of the following is a credential category? (Choose all that apply.)
questions.explanation: The three standard pillars of multifactor authentication are Knowledge (something you know, like a password), Possession (something you have, like a smart card), and Inherence (something you are, like a fingerprint or biometric trait).

questions.prompt: Your Linux workstation runs slowly when you use certain applications. You decide to determine how much virtual memory is used when you run these applications. Which of the following commands enables you to determine virtual memory usage?
questions.explanation: The vmstat (Virtual Memory Statistics) command is an administrative monitoring tool in Linux that reports real-time data about system processes, memory usage, paging activity, block IO, and CPU scheduling.
